summary: Evening workload churn causes gradual throughput thinness and 504s on dedicated reservation
description:
Issue summary: NimbusAI reported a gradual degradation of throughput across their dedicated reservation starting around 18:10 UTC on 2026-03-11. Symptoms include rising p95/p99 latency and intermittent 504 timeouts for streaming requests. Impacted routes are generation and chat endpoints.

Observed behavior is a slow-onset capacity thinness (not an instant outage) that persisted ~90 minutes before partial recovery. No single pod crashed; pods showed high memory use and frequent GPU context switches. Autoscaler did not add capacity quickly enough and, when it did, newly scheduled pods were placed on hosts with competing background batch jobs which caused GPU contention.

Customer-reported impact: user-facing errors on production traffic during peak window; perceived service degradation for end-users of NimbusAI chat product.
impact: Customer-facing 504s and p95 latency increase (~3-5x normal) for dedicated reservation during evening traffic spike. A subset of requests timed out, causing downstream user-visible failures in NimbusAI product. Billing unaffected. No data loss reported.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the customer's traffic profile (mixed short/long sequences with ~25% long-seq requests) and ramp to 80-90% of reservation QPS over 10 minutes.
2) Inject background batch jobs on co-located hosts simulating platform maintenance jobs (GPU-heavy kernels at low priority).
3) Observe p95/p99 latency and any streaming disconnects over a 30-120 minute window.
4) Monitor GPU context-switch counts, host GPU utilization, and autoscaler decision events in the same timeframe.

investigation_notes: 18:40 - Support acknowledged receipt and opened internal SRE thread (#sre-dedicated).
18:55 - SRE observed slow growth in pending queue and higher-than-expected GPU context-switch rates on several hosts servicing NimbusAI reservation.
19:05 - Autoscaler logs show it recommended +2 replicas at 18:25 but placement was delayed due to brokered capacity and global scheduler backoff (placement_delay metric spiked).
19:20 - When new replicas scheduled, they landed on hosts running low-priority batch jobs (background-maintenance), producing immediate contention and no latency relief.

19:40 - Hypothesis: autoscaler sizing thresholds are conservative for mixed long/short seq traffic, and placement policy does not sufficiently avoid hosts with background GPU load. This causes noisy-neighbor behavior even within a dedicated reservation.
20:15 - Eng ran targeted repro in staging using NimbusAI traffic profile; reproduced p95 spike when co-located batch jobs reached >70% GPU utilization on the same host.
root_cause: Combination of undersized autoscaler thresholds for this customer's mixed workload patterns and placement policy allowing placement on hosts with active background batch jobs. The autoscaler decision was delayed by placement backpressure, and when replicas arrived they suffered GPU contention from noisy background jobs, causing sustained high p95/p99 and timeouts.
resolution:
Short-term workaround: manually scaled the reservation by +3 replicas and drained batch workloads from the 3 most impacted hosts; applied a temporary placement rule to prefer hosts in an isolation pool for NimbusAI reservation.

Medium-term fix: adjust autoscaler sensitivity for mixed-length workloads, introduce a placement anti-affinity rule to avoid scheduling on hosts with background-batch label, and add a placement pre-check that rejects hosts with GPU_util>75% for the previous 2 minutes.

Follow-ups: engineering ticket created to update autoscaler heuristics and placement filters (see linked PRs). Notifying NimbusAI of actions and offering a post-incident review.
